culture.title: The Lippitt House Time Capsule
culture.description: An 1865 Victorian built for a governor and barely altered since — original faux-grained woodwork, gasoliers and stencilling, which almost nowhere else still has.
culture.bonus: Find the place where the painted wood stops pretending.

culture.title: Inside the John Brown House
culture.description: A 1788 mansion John Quincy Adams called the most magnificent in North America, now a museum that does not flinch from how the Brown family money was made.
culture.bonus: Ask the guide directly about the slave trade.

culture.title: PVDFest in the Streets
culture.description: The city closes downtown for a weekend of street performance, installations and music — the civic festival that grew out of the WaterFire habit.
culture.bonus: Watch one act all the way through instead of drifting.

culture.title: A Production at Trinity Rep
culture.description: A Tony-winning resident company in a converted 1917 vaudeville house, with a permanent acting ensemble and a willingness to rewrite the classics.
culture.bonus: Read nothing about the play before you walk in.

culture.title: Touring Show at PPAC
culture.description: A 1928 Loew's movie palace with three thousand seats, gilt everywhere and a ceiling worth the ticket on its own, now the city's Broadway house.
culture.bonus: Get there early enough to walk the whole lobby before the house opens.

culture.title: The Collection at the RISD Museum
culture.description: An art school's museum with no business being this good — a Monet, a Manet, Roman bronzes, a 12th-century Japanese Buddha, and a world-class textile collection.
culture.bonus: Find the Buddha and stand with it alone.

culture.title: Exhibition at the WaterFire Arts Center
culture.description: A 1929 steel mill turned into a vast single-room gallery in the Valley, where the scale of the building is half the point of whatever is hanging in it.
culture.bonus: Stand in the far corner and take in the whole room at once.

culture.title: Where Religious Liberty Started
culture.description: A small national memorial on the spring where Roger Williams founded a colony on the then-radical premise that the state had no business in anyone's conscience.
culture.bonus: Read the whole interpretive panel. All of it.

foodie.title: Market Crawl on Federal Hill
foodie.description: Atwells Avenue under its bronze pinecone — fresh ravioli, imported salumi and a market counter where the pasta is made on site.
foodie.bonus: Buy fresh pasta and cook it the same night.

foodie.title: Grilled Pizza at Al Forno
foodie.description: The restaurant that invented grilled pizza in 1980 and still fires it over coals, plus a baked pasta that takes an hour and is worth every minute.
foodie.bonus: Order the Dirty Steak and let them explain why it's called that.

foodie.title: Peruvian Dinner at Los Andes
foodie.description: Peruvian and Bolivian cooking that has outgrown its neighbourhood several times over — ceviche, lomo saltado and portions built for sharing.
foodie.bonus: Order a pisco sour and a ceviche before you look at anything else.

foodie.title: Doughnuts at Knead
foodie.description: Scratch-made doughnuts behind a big glass window in Downcity, with seasonal flavours that change faster than you can get through them.
foodie.bonus: Order the weirdest seasonal flavour on the board.

foodie.title: Fried Clams at Dune Brothers
foodie.description: A seafood shack that started in a shipping container and now runs a proper market — whole-belly clams, day-boat fish, nothing shipped from far away.
foodie.bonus: Order whole-belly clams, not strips. No negotiation.

foodie.title: Midnight at Haven Brothers
foodie.description: A 1949 diner car towed to the kerb beside City Hall every evening since 1893 — the oldest mobile diner in America, and the city's great social leveller.
foodie.bonus: Climb inside and eat at the counter rather than taking it away.

foodie.title: Stall Crawl at Track 15
foodie.description: Seven kitchens and a long central bar inside the restored Union Station, under exposed brick barrel vaults, on tables made from old boxcar flooring.
foodie.bonus: Order from three different stalls and eat it all at one table.

foodie.title: Dinner on DePasquale Plaza
foodie.description: Outdoor tables around the fountain in the middle of Federal Hill, with a Sicilian menu and the whole plaza eating alongside you.
foodie.bonus: Eat outside on the plaza, even if the weather is arguable.

foodie.title: Hand-Rolled Pasta at Oberlin
foodie.description: A tight Westminster Street room doing a small raw bar and some of the best pasta in New England — a James Beard Outstanding Restaurant finalist.
foodie.bonus: Walk in and take a counter seat rather than booking a table.

foodie.title: Ramen and Cocktails at Pickerel
foodie.description: A tiny West End bar with one booth, three ramen on the menu and a cocktail programme that takes itself just seriously enough.
foodie.bonus: Get there at opening — there are almost no seats and no reservations.

foodie.title: Dinner at Nick's on Broadway
foodie.description: Twenty-plus years of Derek Wagner cooking almost everything from Rhode Island farms and boats, in a West Side room that grew out of an 18-seat counter.
foodie.bonus: Ask which farm the vegetables came from and look it up later.

foodie.title: Hot Wieners All the Way at Olneyville
foodie.description: Rhode Island's own creation — a small wiener in a steamed bun with meat sauce, mustard, onion and celery salt, lined up along a counterman's forearm.
foodie.bonus: Order three all the way and a coffee milk, and finish all of it.

adventure.title: Surf Narragansett Town Beach
adventure.description: New England's most reliable beach break, forty minutes south — a long sandy peak that works for beginners and still holds up when a hurricane swell arrives.
adventure.bonus: Stay out until you stand up on a wave you actually chose.

adventure.title: Sunset from Prospect Terrace
adventure.description: A small College Hill park where Roger Williams is buried under a granite statue looking straight out over the downtown skyline he founded.
adventure.bonus: Get there early enough to claim the wall directly below the statue.

adventure.title: Swim Olney Pond at Lincoln Woods
adventure.description: A real swimming pond with a sand beach, fifteen minutes from downtown, surrounded by the same woods the boulderers are working in.
adventure.bonus: Swim out to the buoy line and back without stopping.

adventure.title: Walk the Point at Sachuest
adventure.description: A wildlife refuge on a rocky peninsula past Newport, with harbour seals hauled out on the rocks all winter and surf hitting three sides of the loop.
adventure.bonus: Spot a seal before anyone else in your group does.

adventure.title: Ride the East Bay Bike Path to Bristol
adventure.description: Fourteen and a half miles of old rail bed hugging Narragansett Bay from India Point all the way to Bristol harbour, with water on your right the whole way.
adventure.bonus: Ride the full length and eat something in Bristol before turning back.

adventure.title: Climbing Session at Rock Spot
adventure.description: Rhode Island's climbing hub, with routes and boulder problems set weekly and a crowd that will spot you whether you asked or not.
adventure.bonus: Ask a regular to give you a problem and try it.

adventure.title: Take the Ferry Down to Newport
adventure.description: An hour on the water from downtown Providence, under the Pell Bridge and straight into Newport harbour — the only sensible way to make the trip.
adventure.bonus: Stay on the open top deck the entire crossing, whatever the wind does.

adventure.title: Walk the Newport Cliff Walk
adventure.description: A public path wedged between Gilded Age mansion lawns and the open Atlantic — waves below on one side, The Breakers on the other.
adventure.bonus: Count the Forty Steps on the way down and again on the way up.

adventure.title: Find Lovecraft at Swan Point
adventure.description: A vast Victorian garden cemetery on a bluff over the Seekonk, holding H.P. Lovecraft's grave and its famous inscription — I AM PROVIDENCE.
adventure.bonus: Find the stone without looking up directions first.

adventure.title: Ride the Blackstone River Bikeway
adventure.description: North out of the city along the river that started American industry, past the Slater Mill and up through the old Blackstone Valley towns.
adventure.bonus: Get as far up the valley as you can before you have to turn for home.

adventure.title: Lap Blackstone Boulevard
adventure.description: A wide gravel path down the middle of the East Side's grandest avenue — where all of Providence runs, walks its dogs and judges the architecture.
adventure.bonus: Pick the house you'd buy and commit to it out loud.

adventure.title: Cross the Providence Pedestrian Bridge
adventure.description: A bridge built on the old highway piers purely for walking, with built-in benches and steps down to the water on both banks of the river.
adventure.bonus: Sit on the wooden steps right at the waterline until the light goes.

adventure.title: Loop Roger Williams Park
adventure.description: Four hundred acres of Olmsted-era lakes, bridges and bandstands on the city's south side — a nineteenth-century idea of a park, still working.
adventure.bonus: Walk the full perimeter of all the ponds without shortcuts.

adventure.title: Eighty Braziers Burning at WaterFire
adventure.description: More than eighty bonfires lit on the rivers running through downtown, tended by black-clad boat crews to a soundtrack of world music, from sunset to midnight.
adventure.bonus: Follow a brazier boat on foot for one full pass of the river.

adventure.title: Boulder the Glacial Blocks at Lincoln Woods
adventure.description: New England's most accessible bouldering — hundreds of glacier-dumped granite blocks scattered through oak woods fifteen minutes from downtown.
adventure.bonus: Send a problem you had to try more than three times.

adventure.title: Ride the Woonasquatucket Greenway
adventure.description: A bike path following a once-dead industrial river out of downtown past mill buildings, murals and the reclaimed riverbanks behind them.
adventure.bonus: Stop at every mural you can see from the path.

social.title: Kennedy Plaza After Dark
social.description: The city's crossroads at night — the skating rink in winter, events in summer, and Haven Brothers parked at the kerb either way.
social.bonus: End the night at the diner window, whatever time it is.

social.title: Late Counter Seat at Pickerel
social.description: Four seats at a wooden bar, cocktails made properly, and a bowl of ramen at eleven at night — the best small room on the West Side.
social.bonus: Go after ten and take whatever seat is free.

social.title: Bluegrass Throedown at Nick-a-Nee's
social.description: A green cinderblock box in the Jewelry District, cash only, jukebox loud, with a Wednesday bluegrass session that has run for decades.
social.bonus: Bring cash. There is no second option.

social.title: Taproom Crawl of the Mills
social.description: Providence's breweries all moved into the same dead textile mills — you can walk between several of them on the West Side in an afternoon.
social.bonus: One pour at each stop, no repeats, no favourites.

social.title: Show at the Columbus Theatre
social.description: A 1926 Broadway picture palace, half-restored and gloriously faded, now one of the best-sounding rooms for touring songwriters in New England.
social.bonus: Sit in the balcony for at least half the set.

social.title: Atwells Avenue Bar Night
social.description: Federal Hill after dinner — a tight run of wine bars, cafés and late spots under the arch, all within a few hundred metres of each other.
social.bonus: Finish the night with an espresso rather than another drink.

social.title: Loud Night at Fête Music Hall
social.description: A converted Olneyville mill with two rooms running at once — you can usually find a show you want and a second one you didn't know about.
social.bonus: Check out whatever is happening in the other room mid-set.

social.title: Cocktails at The Eddy
social.description: The city's reference cocktail bar since 2012 — dark, narrow, serious about the classics, and willing to make you something off-menu if you let it.
social.bonus: Name a spirit and a mood and drink whatever arrives.

social.title: P-Bruins at the Amica Mutual Pavilion
social.description: Minor league hockey in a downtown arena where the crowd is close, loud and entirely unbothered about whether this is the NHL.
social.bonus: Stay standing for the whole of a power play.

social.title: Opening Night at an AS220 Gallery
social.description: An unjuried, uncensored artist collective running three downtown galleries, where the opening receptions are the actual social event.
social.bonus: Talk to one artist about their own piece before you leave.

social.title: Pints at the Rebuilt Trinity Brewhouse
social.description: Providence's longtime brewpub beside the theatre district, reopened in 2026 under new owners with a new brewer and the beer still made on site.
social.bonus: Order the house beer you've never seen anywhere else.

social.title: Pop-Up Dinner Night at Long Live
social.description: The brewery hands its kitchen corner to a different cook most weeks — go without checking who it is and eat whatever they brought.
social.bonus: Don't look up the pop-up beforehand.

chill.title: Eighteen Taps at Long Live Beerworks
chill.description: A restored mill taproom on the West Side pouring inventive IPAs, sours and stouts, with a rotating food pop-up in the corner.
chill.bonus: Drink the sour even if you think you don't like sours.

chill.title: A Drink Among the Shelves at Riffraff
chill.description: A small bookshop with a proper bar in it, heavy on translated fiction, where the staff will talk you into something you've never heard of.
chill.bonus: Buy the book the bartender recommends.

chill.title: Wander Wickenden Street
chill.description: Fox Point's main street — Portuguese bakeries, record shops, coffee and junk stores in a few walkable blocks near the water.
chill.bonus: Go into the shop you'd normally walk past.

chill.title: Read in the Providence Athenaeum
chill.description: An 1838 Greek Revival library on Benefit Street where Poe courted Sarah Helen Whitman — open stacks, green lamps, and absolutely no reason to hurry.
chill.bonus: Pull a book published before 1900 and read a page of it.

chill.title: Narragansetts at the Hot Club
chill.description: A family-run waterfront dive of nearly forty years on the Providence River, where the correct order is a cold can and a seat facing the hurricane barrier.
chill.bonus: Be on the deck when the neon flashes at 8:30.

chill.title: Sit by the Basin at Waterplace Park
chill.description: A Venetian-style tidal basin with stepped stone amphitheatre seating, built where a parking lot and a covered river used to be.
chill.bonus: Walk the whole ring of the basin at water level.

chill.title: Walk the Mile of History on Benefit Street
chill.description: One of the densest surviving stretches of colonial architecture in America — gas lamps, cobbles, and the houses Lovecraft put straight into his stories.
chill.bonus: Find the oldest date carved on any house on the street.

chill.title: Warm Up in the Botanical Center
chill.description: The largest indoor display garden in New England — two glasshouses of palms and orchids that stay humid and green while Rhode Island freezes outside.
chill.bonus: Go on the coldest day of the year.

chill.title: Walk Through the Van Wickle Gates
chill.description: Brown's 1764 campus on College Hill — brick quads, enormous trees, and iron gates that by tradition only open twice a year.
chill.bonus: Sit on the Quiet Green with no phone for fifteen minutes.

chill.title: Watch the Bay from India Point Park
chill.description: Where the river opens into Narragansett Bay — a long grassy waterfront with the hurricane barrier on one side and open water on the other.
chill.bonus: Stay until you've watched a boat go all the way out of sight.

8ball.title: The Rhode Island Trinity
8ball.description: Wildcard: in one day, eat a hot wiener all the way, drink a coffee milk, and get a plate of whole-belly clams. Three things this state has and almost nowhere else does.
8ball.bonus: Do all three before the sun goes down.

8ball.title: I Am Providence
8ball.description: Wildcard: walk Lovecraft's Providence on foot — Benefit Street, the Athenaeum, Prospect Terrace, and finally his headstone at Swan Point — and read one of his stories after dark.
